\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اختیار} (ikhtiyār)}{اختیار (ikhtiyār)}]{\ur{اختیار} (ikhtiyār) — authority; a power (to decide)}

\label{lesson:UR-C339-ikhtiyar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to enumerate, then the Urdu for a reference.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اختیار}}
\textbf{\ur{اختیار}} — \emph{ikhtiyār} — \textquotedblleft{}authority; a power (to decide)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{یہ} \ur{میرے} \ur{اختیار} \ur{میں} \ur{نہیں} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yih mere ikhtiyār meṅ nahīṅ hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This is not in my power.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اختیار}} (\emph{ikhtiyār}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ikhtiyār}, \textquotedblleft{}choice\textquotedblright{}: the power to choose.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ikhtiyār}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ikhtiyār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yih mere ikhtiyār meṅ nahīṅ hai.} — This is not in my power.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to enumerate, then the Urdu for a reference, then say \emph{ikhtiyār} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{اختیار} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Authority; a power (to decide)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{عمل} \ur{کرنا} (amal karnā)}{عمل کرنا (amal karnā)}]{\ur{عمل} \ur{کرنا} (amal karnā) — to act on; to follow (a rule, advice)}

\label{lesson:UR-C339-amal-karna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for justice, then the Urdu for suitable.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{عمل} \ur{کرنا}}
\textbf{\ur{عمل} \ur{کرنا}} — \emph{amal karnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to act on; to follow (a rule, advice)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ہمیں} \ur{قانون} \ur{پر} \ur{عمل} \ur{کرنا} \ur{چاہیے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hameṅ qānūn par amal karnā chāhiye.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We should keep to the law.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{مشورے} \ur{پر} \ur{عمل} \ur{کیا}, \emph{us ne mashvare par amal kiyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{عمل} \ur{کرنا}} (\emph{amal karnā}) is built from \emph{amal}, usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ʿamal}, \textquotedblleft{}an action\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ur{کرنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}: to put a rule into action.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ادا} \ur{کرنا} (adā karnā)}{ادا کرنا (adā karnā)}]{\ur{ادا} \ur{کرنا} (adā karnā) — to pay (a debt); to fulfil (a duty)}

\label{lesson:UR-C339-ada-karna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for suitable, then the Urdu for to act on.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ادا} \ur{کرنا}}
\textbf{\ur{ادا} \ur{کرنا}} — \emph{adā karnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to pay (a debt); to fulfil (a duty)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ہر} \ur{شہری} \ur{کو} \ur{اپنا} \ur{فرض} \ur{ادا} \ur{کرنا} \ur{چاہیے۔}

\begin{quote}
\emph{har shahrī ko apnā farz adā karnā chāhiye.}

\begin{quote}
